h1: Furama Silom Bangkok — 4-Star Rooftop Pool on Lower Silom, ~5 Min BTS Saphan Taksin
intro: Looking for a 4-star hotel on the lower stretch of Silom Road where you can walk to BTS Saphan Taksin in five minutes and catch the Chao Phraya Express Boat at Sathorn Pier in the same time? Furama Silom Bangkok sits at 533 Silom Road in Bang Rak, offering 258 rooms, a rooftop swimming pool with views toward King Power Mahanakhon Tower, and access to one of Bangkok's most historically layered neighbourhoods. Score 8.1/10 from 917 reviews on Trip.com. Rooms from approx. ฿1,500/night.

body.html: Furama Silom Bangkok stands at 533 Silom Road in Bang Rak — the lower, quieter end of Silom closest to the Chao Phraya. From the front door, BTS Saphan Taksin is roughly a five-minute walk, and Sathorn Pier (Central Pier) — the main terminal for the Chao Phraya Express Boat network — is the same distance away. That puts virtually every riverside temple and neighbourhood in Bangkok within reach without a taxi: Wat Arun, Tha Chang, Iconsiam, and the Nonthaburi ferry stop are all accessible from the pier. The surrounding Bang Rak area adds its own pull: Bang Rak Market, Assumption College's century-old building on Charoenkrung, and the Haroon riverside community are all short walks away.

The hotel's 258 rooms are dressed in a contemporary Thai palette — floor-to-ceiling windows, warm lighting, and a layout that most guests describe as more spacious than the price tag would suggest. Room categories run from Superior and Deluxe to Executive Club Rooms (with Executive Lounge access providing complimentary breakfast, afternoon snacks, and evening cocktails) and a Family Room option for groups of three to four. Wi-Fi and parking are both complimentary, which is a practical plus for self-drive visitors heading into Bangkok's traffic.

"The rooftop pool was the highlight — the view of Mahanakhon Tower at sunset is genuinely something. The room was bigger than I expected, staff were warm and helpful. For what we paid, it was really solid value in Silom."

The standout facility is the outdoor rooftop pool on the 20th floor, where the views take in King Power Mahanakhon Tower and the Silom skyline. Guests consistently name this as their most-praised feature and — importantly — consistently express surprise that it exists at this price point. The gym, sauna, and massage room complete the leisure offering. RAMA restaurant serves Thai and international food; the breakfast buffet is noted repeatedly in reviews for good variety, with guests generally considering it fair value.

Being honest about the downsides — because this is what real reviews tell us: the building is showing its age. Furama Silom opened in 2009 with a renovation in 2012, and in a city where new hotels open every month, this puts it at a disadvantage on raw modernity. Some rooms have ageing air-conditioning units that can be noisy. Maintenance consistency varies across the property. A minority of guest reviews report cleanliness concerns in bathrooms, and occasional pest sightings have been mentioned — enough to be worth noting rather than glossing over. Slow lifts during check-out rushes also come up frequently.

Against these caveats, the things guests praise consistently are the friendly staff, the rooftop pool, the location score (8.6 on Trip.com — the highest-rated category across all platforms), and the room sizes relative to what you pay. For travellers whose priority is a well-placed 4-star base with a genuine rooftop pool and BTS access at under ฿2,000/night, Furama Silom still delivers a useful package. For travellers who need pristine contemporary rooms and hotel-wide maintenance to a consistently high standard, there are newer properties nearby worth comparing.

Furama Silom Bangkok suits travellers who want a practical Bangkok base on the Silom–Bang Rak stretch: one BTS stop from Silom, five stops from Siam, and the Chao Phraya river boat at the end of the street. Business travellers on short stays who value the Executive Lounge perk, couples who want the rooftop pool without paying 5-star prices, and families who can make use of the Family Room and the proximity to Robinson Bang Rak mall — these are the guests this hotel tends to work best for.

honestSummary: Furama Silom Bangkok is a 4-star hotel where location and the rooftop pool remain the strongest arguments for booking, at a price point that undercuts many competitors in the same area. It is honest to note that the building — opened in 2009 — is not at peak condition throughout, and cleanliness standards across all rooms are not perfectly uniform. It works well for travellers who want a mobile, affordable Silom base rather than a freshly renovated hotel experience.
honestChecks: If cleanliness is a top priority — inspect your room on check-in and do not hesitate to ask for a change if the bathroom falls short. The hotel generally acts on complaints; the mistake is waiting rather than asking immediately.

If you have an early flight or appointment — lifts can be slow during morning check-out rush. Build in an extra 10–15 minutes or take the stairs for lower floors to make your BTS or river boat on time.
If you specifically want the rooftop pool — during peak season the pool fills up by late afternoon. Aim to go mid-morning or early afternoon for a quieter experience with better views.

tips.title: Take the River Boat from Sathorn Pier
tips.body: Sathorn Pier/Central Pier is about a 5-minute walk from the hotel. From there, the Chao Phraya Express Boat reaches Wat Arun, Tha Chang, Tha Maharaj, and Iconsiam — cheaper and far more atmospheric than Grab for riverside sightseeing.

tips.title: Hit the Rooftop Pool at Golden Hour
tips.body: The view of King Power Mahanakhon Tower and the Silom skyline from the 20th-floor pool is best around sunset. Get there by 17:00 before it gets busy — the light on the tower's distinctive pixel-cut facade is genuinely worth seeing.

tips.title: Walk to Robinson Bang Rak for Essentials
tips.body: Robinson / Central Bang Rak mall is an 8-minute walk away and has a Tops supermarket, pharmacies, and a solid range of restaurants at all budgets — convenient for groceries or a relaxed dinner without a taxi.

tips.title: One Stop to Silom, Five to Siam
tips.body: BTS Saphan Taksin is one stop from Silom station and five from Siam — with a Rabbit Card loaded up, you can cover Sukhumvit, the malls, and Chatuchak without touching Grab for most day trips.

faq.q: Where is Furama Silom Bangkok and how far is it from BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 533 Silom Road, Bang Rak, Bangkok 10500 — on the lower stretch of Silom Road nearest the Chao Phraya River. It is approximately a 5-minute walk to BTS Saphan Taksin station and around 5 minutes to Sathorn Pier / Central Pier, the main Chao Phraya Express Boat terminal.

faq.q: What is the starting price for Furama Silom Bangkok?
faq.a: Rooms start from approximately ฿1,500/night for a Superior Room in off-peak periods. Deluxe rooms are around ฿1,800+. Executive Club Rooms with lounge access are around ฿2,400+. The Family Room starts around ฿2,800+. Prices vary by date and platform — compare Agoda, Booking.com, and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Does Furama Silom Bangkok have a swimming pool?
faq.a: Yes — there is an outdoor swimming pool on the 20th floor rooftop, with views of King Power Mahanakhon Tower and the Silom skyline. It is open to all guests and is consistently the most praised feature in guest reviews, particularly mentioned as exceeding expectations for the price.

faq.q: Can I use the Chao Phraya Express Boat from this hotel?
faq.a: Very easily — Sathorn Pier / Central Pier is approximately 5 minutes on foot from the hotel. From there you can take the Chao Phraya Express Boat north to Tha Chang (Wat Pho, Grand Palace), Tha Maharaj, and Nonthaburi, or south toward Iconsiam. It is one of the best and most cost-effective ways to sightsee from this location.

faq.q: Is Furama Silom Bangkok suitable for families?
faq.a: Yes, reasonably so — there is a Family Room with two King beds that suits groups of three to four. The rooftop pool is a bonus for children. Robinson / Central Bang Rak mall is a short walk away with restaurants at multiple price points. Specify a Family Room at booking and request a higher floor for better views and less street noise.
